comparisonPolicy: The exact CC BY-SA Commons PNG is the primary live-fish target and was visually inspected directly. The second exact Commons page corroborates the side profile only. FishBase governs taxonomy and morphometrics. No reference pixels are copied, sampled, traced, embedded, redistributed, or hotlinked.

primaryTarget.notes: The actual image visibly confirms extreme lateral compression, a steep forehead into a small terminal mouth, tall swept dorsal and anal fins, a narrow tail base, long threadlike pelvic filaments, warm eye and fin accents, and dark adult bars. Because it is oblique rather than orthographic, it does not by itself calibrate total side length.

side.notes: The primary Commons PNG is front-left oblique, while FishBase and the second exact Commons page corroborate the side profile. Together they constrain the tall triangular envelope, concave forehead, small terminal mouth, swept median fins, narrow caudal, elongated pelvic rays, and four adult bars.

top.uncertainty: High. No verified true orthographic whole-fish top photograph was found; half-width stations only implement FishBase's highly compressed classification.
top.notes: Top width is intentionally conservative and must remain visually reviewable rather than treated as measured.

front.uncertainty: High. No verified true orthographic frontal photograph was found; head width, eye seating, and terminal lip volume are inferred from compressed-body classification and lateral imagery.
front.notes: The front profile cannot be accepted as source-measured until a verified frontal original is added.

silhouetteLandmarks.name: highly compressed disc/diamond trunk and concave dorsal head
silhouetteLandmarks.notes: Deep anal-level stations, narrow half-widths, and a forehead saddle before the terminal snout prevent a generic oval cichlid or marine-angelfish profile.

silhouetteLandmarks.name: tall triangular dorsal and anal envelopes with long first branched rays
silhouetteLandmarks.notes: Posterior-increasing spines lead into the tallest early soft rays, then taper to the peduncle, forming the characteristic upper and lower triangles.

silhouetteLandmarks.name: narrow caudal and elongated thoracic pelvic rays
silhouetteLandmarks.notes: A restrained caudal fan avoids a generic broad tail, while narrow paired pelvic roots and long distal filaments extend from the thorax.

proportions.name: maximum adult total length
proportions.notes: The 84 mm station-defined standard length plus the unchanged 21 mm caudal reach targets FishBase's 10.5 cm total length.

proportions.name: standard length divided by body height at anal level
proportions.notes: The source evaluates to 0.084 / (0.038 + 0.036) = 1.135, inside FishBase's 1.07 to 1.29 range.

proportions.name: maximum width divided by anal-level body height
proportions.uncertainty: High. FishBase establishes compression but does not provide a calibrated width, and no true orthographic top view was found.
proportions.notes: The visually inspected oblique primary supports stronger lateral compression than fable-v2, while the exact numeric width remains explicitly provisional.

colorPatternBoundaries.name: adult four-bar silver pattern
colorPatternBoundaries.notes: Four procedural dark bars cross the eye, shoulder, midbody, and caudal base; the seven-bar juvenile pattern is explicitly excluded.

colorPatternBoundaries.name: silver-olive body with restrained warm eye and fin cues
colorPatternBoundaries.notes: Silver flank sheen, restrained olive dorsum, pale belly, warm throat and fin rays, and translucent membranes are generated procedurally with fixed seeds.

reviewedCandidate.notes: The technically valid fable-v2 candidate was visually rejected after in-tank review. Its body remains too inflated, caudal too broad, median fins too rounded and rigid, pelvic filaments too thick, face too bead-like, and silver-bar finish too generic for the actual Pterophyllum target.

previousCandidate.notes: The technically valid v1 render was visually rejected because its forked triangular tail, stepped blunt head, monolithic median fins, thick pelvic spears, oversized pectorals, opaque cream body, and mechanical bars contradicted the recorded adult references.

repairCandidate.notes: Future fable-v3 strengthens the diagnostic Pterophyllum silhouette with a thinner body, steeper forehead, smaller seated eye and mouth, taller swept dorsal and anal envelopes, narrower caudal, longer threadlike pelvic filaments, brighter silver body, organic adult bars, and restrained warm eye and fin accents.

mismatches.note: Rejected: v2 remains too wide and oval from side and front. V3 must read as an extremely laterally compressed, tall scalare body rather than a generic disc cichlid.
Rejected: v2 median fins are broad rounded sails and the caudal is oversized. V3 must show tall swept dorsal and anal triangles, a narrow caudal, and threadlike pelvic filaments.

Rejected: v2 retains a bead-like eye, blunt mouth, flat grey finish, and mechanical bars. V3 must have a steep forehead, small terminal mouth, seated warm eye, silver flank, and organic correctly positioned adult bars.
